basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 4.' and it opens '(Ver. 4.) Et respexit Deus super Abel, et super munera ejus: super Cain autem et super'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Ver. 4.) Et respexit Deus super Abel, et super munera ejus: super Cain autem et super sacrificia ejus non respexit, et contristatus est Cain valde. Unde scire poterat Cain, quod fratris munera suscepisset Deus, et sua repudiasset: nisi illa interpretatio vera est, quam Theodotion posuit. Et inflammavit Dominus super Abel, et super sacrificium ejus: super Cain vero, et super sacrificium ejus non inflammavit. Ignem autem ad sacrificium devorandum solitum venire de coelo: et in dedicatione templi sub Salomone legimus, et quando Elias in monte Carmelo construxit altare (II Par. VII, 1; III Reg. XVIII, 38).
